programmes.d: In the 1990s, the media dubbed Richard Rogers the "Last Call Killer" because he targeted men in gay bars who were obviously intoxicated.
A woman's body is found inside a burned mobile home and the autopsy reveals she was beaten.
After a street fight takes the life of a national wrestling champion, police must determine if he was killed in cold blood or in self-defense.
A mother and her two young daughters are found brutally murdered and sexually violated.

When a college student is reported missing, police believe their investigation will be like countless others. But when they discover blood spatter in her boyfriend's bedroom, they know this case is going to be different.
In 2008, college co-ed Jenna Verhaalen was found dead in her Bryan, Texas apartment.
The killer hoped to cover his tracks by staging the crime scene. But police saw through the attempt.
An assistant manager of a Florida steakhouse is stabbed to death. It appears to be a robbery gone wrong, but a bloody fingerprint reveals that he knew his killer.
Pathologist examining death of politician running for re-election finds puncture wounds at autopsy.

Bombings are difficult to solve because the perpetrator isn't usually at the scene and the evidence goes up in smoke. In this case, pieces of plastic the size of grains of sand hold the key to finding a murderer.

Two men are murdered while sleeping in their beds. The next night, arson destroys a family planning clinic. Investigators wonder whether some shards of glass, paint chips and a chicken feather could link what appear to be two separate crimes.
When an off-duty policeman was shot dead, his fellow officers were determined to solve the crime.
Investigating a Colorado hunter shot and killed; police suspect two murder weapons and two killers.
In 1981, New York correctional officer Donna Payant disappeared and was later found in a landfill. The medical examiner not only identified the cause of death, but also found an important clue.
In 2000, construction manager Darrell North was found dead in his work trailer in Ft. Worth, Texas.
The wife of a respected police officer was murdered in her own home. The crime went unsolved for more than a decade, until a newly formed cold case unit took a fresh look at the evidence.
When two women were found brutally murdered, police wondered if they were victims of a hate crime.
In 1987, a human skull and some bones were discovered at a Boy Scout Camp near Farmington, Missouri. Facial reconstruction aids the investigators in this case.
When anomalies stall a murder case, a candy wrapper and seeds help expose the killer.

This killer probably hoped to cover his tracks by staging the crime scene. But investigators saw through the attempt almost immediately and turned to forensic science to learn what really happened that night.
On May 20, 2001, Carrie Nelson, then 20, was beaten to death while working alone in a park office.
In 2003, Kathy Lorick was murdered on a Concord, California jogging trail while talking to her husband on her mobile phone.
The disappearance of a mail-order bride is suspicious when police learn of the husband's past wives.
An investigation into the murder of Katie Poirier is stymied by the lack of a body. Finally, investigators use a single tooth found among some charred remains to identify her.
In 2006, Darlene VanderGiesen received threatening emails and then disappeared.

A young TV news producer is raped and murdered in her apartment. Police identify two suspects, but both are cleared of any wrongdoing. When the case stalls for more than a year, investigators turn to the Commonwealth of Virginia's DNA Databank.
After inspecting storm damage to a home in Tampa, an insurance assessor simply disappeared.

The doctors at the hospital couldn't determine the cause of Bobby Curley's hallucinations and intense pain. They treated it as a neurological disorder but his condition deteriorated. He was being poisoned.
A son searches for the truth when his mother is charged with the murder of his father.
In 1985, Julie Estes was kidnapped from the Southside convenience store where she worked. Her body was found the next day, but the killing went unsolved until 2003.
The 1996 investigation into 48-year-old Martha Hansen's murder is helped by a legal requirement.
While investigating the murder of 9-year-old Jessica Knott, police use a garbage bag to connect suspect James Edward Crow, Jr. to the crime.
Eyewitnesses description don't come close to resembling the prime suspect.
After 6-year-old Michelle Lee Dorr went missing, her father confessed to murdering her. But investigators soon poked holes in his story, leaving the case unsolved for 14 years.
In 2004, nursing student Tamika Huston went missing from her Spartanburg, South Carolina home.

In 1988, the body of a young woman was discovered in an Ohio river. Most of the evidence had been washed away, but the victim's 6-year-old son unwittingly told investigators all they needed to know — without saying a word. The clue was in his genes.
A union official is executed in his home not long after a strike by the union membership.

In 1999, Susan Fassett was gunned down as she left her church choir practice in Poughkeepsie, NY. After clearing her husband, police turned their attention to Fred Andros, with whom Susan had an affair.
Moments before she dies, a woman writes a name on a wall with her blood.

An investigation into the murder of a World War II veteran slowed to a halt when the prime suspect had a solid alibi. But a lucky break led to a shady character who wore distinctive boots and had a sweet tooth.
Tipster is found dead after revealing that a woman's death 16 years ago was murder.
Haunted by the disappearance of her mother, a young woman undertakes an investigation of her own. In her mother's diary, she discovers a dark family secret that might explain the disappearance.
A young girl with no ID is found on an isolated farm but has mailbox and house keys.
In 1998, a Maryland murder mystery performance turns into a real whodunit when the badly burned body of Stephen Hricko is discovered in his hotel room.
Garbage bag leads to a killer.

The woman was dead. The man had been shot four times and survived. When the man's version of events contradicted physical evidence, investigators turned to forensic science to paint a clearer picture of the crime.
When a popular disc jockey was found murdered in a community garden, police swung into action.

Emergency dispatch received a call from a man who said his girlfriend shot and killed herself. The autopsy revealed that the gunshot wound was not self-inflicted, and the evidence on her body would give police a golden opportunity to catch her killer.
In 1994, a human skull retrieved from an Ohio pond reveals a ghastly crime.
When a woman went missing, friends and family were determined to find her. Their worst fears were confirmed weeks later when her body was discovered.
Investigators reassemble a 5-1/4 computer disk cut to pieces with pinking shears to find murderer.
The decade-old murder of a young Texas housewife is investigated.

When Joann Katrinak is found dead in a corn field with her infant son, the obvious suspect is the husband and father of the victims. But insects found on the bodies reveal a vital clue which uncovers a twisted story of passion gone wrong.
A suspect's former lover comes forward with a tale of murder, mutilation and cremation.

A go-go dancer told her family she needed to get away for a while and then she simply disappeared. Investigators were suspicious, because she took neither her car nor her clothes. 20 years later, her family received a call that changed everything.
Police investigate a Native American woman's murder less than 10 miles from another murder scene.
On May 12, 1994, Crystal Perry was viciously murdered in her home in Bridgton, Maine. Michael Hutchinson, 32, was later found guilty in the slaying.
A week after a couple disappears from the beach, police get a mysterious lead from a robbery.

A behavioral profile caused the Baton Rouge Police Department to search for the wrong man. The real perpetrator may have eluded arrest, had it not been for a molecular biologist who painted DNA picture of the suspect.

In 1988, when a patient dies unexpectedly in the office of California neurologist Richard Boggs, police begin what they think will be a routine investigation. Soon they uncover a bizarre story of corpse stealing, fake identity and sexual perversion.
A bomb kills a man and a painstaking search yields tiny clues which precisely identify the killer.
Forensic developments reveal new facts in the case of a man convicted of sexual assault.
In 2003, St. Cloud teenager Jason MacLennan returned home after a night out with friends and discovered his father's body lying in a pool of blood.
A 1995 fire razes the mansion of a Kansas doctor, killing two of her three children.

In 1993, the state of Florida was known for more than just Disney World. Worldwide attention focused on a rash of robberies which targeted tourists. Some vacationers were killed in these attacks, but some fought and survived.
Investigators use the recollections of a child to determine what happened to a missing woman.
Police get a clue about a couple who disappeared on Memorial Day weekend during an in-progress robbery. The evidence found solves a brutal crime.
A millionaire and his family were executed in their own home.

How unlucky could one man be? His college sweetheart killed herself and fourteen years later, his wife ended her life in a similar way. Investigators had to determine if this was murder or simply a bizarre coincidence.
Woman disappears from grocery store parking lot in Boulder; investigators find extraordinary clues.

Investigators sift through the ashes of a fire which killed a 40-year-old woman. The fire appears to have been started by an unattended cigarette. On closer look, forensic scientists discover the cause was far more complicated.
Aspiring model's death points to her boyfriend who is soon cleared.
A college senior was found raped and murdered near an unpaved footpath used by students to walk from one side of campus to the other.
A forensic scientist uses his skills to preserve a footprint left in snow.

In 1994, 19-year-old Shannon Melendi disappeared while at Emory University. Her disappearance remained a mystery for ten years, until new scientific testing cast a different light on Colvin "Butch" Hinton.
A suspect's former lover comes forward with a tale of murder, mutilation and cremation.

When investigators found Bruce Miller dead in the office of his junkyard business, the crime scene was almost pristine. But when a computer forensics expert examined computers owned by the victim's wife and her lover, he found all the evidence needed.
A pair of tennis shoes are found near a victim who had been stabbed on the beach.
Police are dispatched to the scene of a shooting and discover the victim's husband is one of their own: a homicide detective who says his wife accidentally shot herself in the head.
After inspecting storm damage to a home in Tampa, an insurance assessor simply disappeared.
When the body of a young woman is found under an isolated highway ramp, a unique fiber on the victim's clothing leads San Diego police straight to the most unlikely of killers.
Investigators look into the death of a teacher and discover that his death was not an accident.
When two women went missing and were later found brutally murdered, police wondered if they were victims of a hate crime.
Using an anonymous letter and geographical profiling, investigators close in on a serial rapist.
In 1991, when the wife of a serviceman was brutally murdered in the Philippines, investigators had to reassemble a tiny computer disk that had been cut to pieces in order to find the killer.
A woman convicted of killing her mother in a car fire is granted a new trial.
Doctors don't know why a young scientist has fallen gravely ill. When tests finally reveal the cause, it's too late to save him.
Crystal Faye Todd's case is examined; the popular high school student was raped and murdered.
A serial rapist is on the loose in a Texas town. No one knew where he'd strike next, but the audacity of his attacks and the escalation of violence against his victims made finding him imperative.
Investigators reassemble a 5-1/4 computer disk cut to pieces with pinking shears to find murderer.
In 2004, nursing student Tamika Huston went missing from her Spartanburg, South Carolina home. A tip led detectives to her car, where they found an unknown house key that could help solve the case.
Police uncover deleted computer files during an investigation.

In 2006, Nevada politician Kathy Augustine died mysteriously during a re-election campaign. The medical examiner could neither isolate the cause of death, nor explain the tiny puncture wounds discovered during the autopsy.
A computer crash pushed a manufacturing company to the brink of collapse. Was it sabotage?

A woman is reported missing after a fight with her husband. Police suspect a man who reported a fire in his car. Two tiny drops of blood are found in the interior. Finally, a tiny clue inside the suspect's watchband helps solve the case.
When a dedicated teacher disappeared, police had to determine if she was the victim of foul play.

When a popular disc jockey was found murdered in a community garden, police swung into action. A sniffer dog and a blood spatter expert led police to the killer, who had been much closer than they realized.
A three-year-old develops a respiratory condition. His father has Alzheimers.

Lack of evidence compels investigators to look beyond the obvious when a woman is beaten to death.
